Why it is the best next use of budget: it builds on the strongest result so far while answering a broad design question in a clean way. Changing the encoder or adding fusion now would answer a narrower question or vary several choices at once.

This experiment keeps the best configuration (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000) and changes only avgpool to transformer, which isolates the effect of the aggregation method. That makes it a cheap, clean exploitation step. Its result will tell us which aggregation to carry into later encoder and multimodal comparisons, so it is a good use of the limited budget before those choices multiply the search space.

We do not yet know whether image features add complementary signal or only add noise. This experiment adds ResNet50 images to the best known setup (PCA, multiprofile, avgpool) using simple concat fusion, changing a single factor relative to config_002. If it beats 0.688, the multimodal branch is worth exploring further, including weighted fusion and ViT-L. If it does not, we can deprioritize much of the multimodal space and spend the remaining budget on RNA encoders such as scGPT. That makes it the most uncertainty-reducing experiment for the budget.

ResNet50 image-only was weak (0.227), and adding it by concat fusion lowered performance to 0.532. scGPT, the third RNA encoder, is still untested in the strongest setting. 2) This experiment changes only the RNA encoder from the current best (config_002), swapping PCA for scGPT while keeping multiprofile and avgpool. It completes the encoder comparison and shows whether a pretrained foundation-model embedding beats PCA. 3) This is a clean one-factor test on the strongest RNA-only setting, so it can either produce a new best model or confirm that PCA is the right RNA backbone. Either result guides later multimodal tests. Those would more sensibly try weighted fusion or the ViT-L image encoder on top of the best RNA encoder, rather than spend more budget on combinations that keep the weak image branch now.

It is unclear whether multimodal fails because image features carry little signal or because naive concatenation lets noisy image features dilute the strong RNA signal. 2. If it stays near 0.53 or below, ResNet50 image features likely hurt regardless of fusion, which argues for trying ViT-L or focusing on RNA-only. 3. Why now: with a limited budget, this one controlled comparison decides whether the large multimodal part of the search space deserves further experiments, while staying anchored to the best-performing RNA setup.

1. Evidence and uncertainty: The best result so far is RNA-only multiprofile PCA with avgpool (config_002, acc 0.688). With PCA, it lowered accuracy from 0.688 to 0.650. Two things remain unclear: whether the weighted-fusion advantage is general, and whether images ever add value to RNA. 2. What this tests: config_031 adds ResNet50 images with weighted fusion to the scVI multiprofile avgpool model (config_005, acc 0.635). That is a single-change comparison against config_005, isolating whether images help an scVI RNA branch. It also differs from config_019 only in the RNA encoder, which shows whether the weighted-fusion gain carries over across RNA encoders. 3. Why it is the best use of budget: It reuses the strongest known settings (multiprofile, avgpool, weighted fusion) and has a realistic chance of a competitive score. It also directly reduces uncertainty about the central question of whether multimodal fusion beats RNA-only. Each outcome is informative: a gain over 0.635 would support pursuing fusion further, while a drop would strengthen the case for RNA-only modeling.

1. Evidence and uncertainty: scGPT RNA-only (config_007) is clearly the best result so far (acc 0.586, F1 0.574). Evidence: we have only two single-profile baselines. RNA (PCA) reached 0.678 accuracy and 0.646 F1. Image (ResNet50) reached 0.619 accuracy and 0.610 F1. 1) Evidence: RNA-only with PCA reached 0.678 accuracy and image-only with ResNet50 reached 0.619. Concat fusion of those same two encoders collapsed to 0.224 accuracy and 0.184 F1, far below either single modality. 1. Evidence: The best result so far is RNA-only multiprofile PCA with avgpool (0.639 accuracy, 0.620 F1). PCA beat scVI and scGPT, and avgpool beat the transformer. Adding ResNet50 image features lowered performance (concat 0.535, weighted 0.512). This is likely because ResNet50 images alone are weak (0.227). The ImageNet ViT-L encoder is the largest untested design axis, so we cannot yet tell whether multimodal fusion fails in general or only with a weak image encoder. 2. Test: config_024 differs from config_018 only in the image encoder (ViT-L instead of ResNet50). It keeps the best RNA encoder, aggregation and fusion settings, so the result isolates the effect of image representation in the fusion setting. 3. Why now: Under a limited budget, this one run checks whether stronger image features help or hurt fusion, and it also has a plausible chance of beating the RNA-only best. If it still trails RNA-only, that is strong evidence to deprioritize the many remaining multimodal configurations.

1. Evidence: the best result so far is config_024 (PCA + ImageNet ViT-L, multiprofile, avgpool, concat) at 0.688 accuracy and 0.659 F1. That beats RNA-only avgpool (0.639). Multimodal fusion with ResNet50 instead hurt performance (0.535 and 0.512). This points to the image representation as the deciding factor, but no ViT-L image-only model has been run. The only image-only baseline is ResNet50 single-profile, which was weak (0.227). 2. Test: config_014 is the ViT-L image-only counterpart of config_024, keeping multiprofile and avgpool the same. It will show whether ViT-L features are strong on their own, or whether the gain in config_024 comes from them complementing PCA RNA features. 3. Why now: this isolates the image-encoder effect within the current best setting, before spending budget on fusion or aggregation variants of config_024. Its result will guide later choices, such as whether to try weighted fusion or transformer aggregation with ViT-L.

1. Evidence: Only one result exists, the RNA-only, single-profile, PCA baseline (accuracy 0.725, F1 0.685). We do not yet know how any design factor affects performance. 2. What this tests: config_002 changes only one thing, switching from single-profile to multi-profile with the simplest aggregation (avgpool), while keeping the modality and RNA encoder fixed. 1. Evidence: Only RNA-only PCA models have been tested. 1. Evidence: RNA-only with PCA is clearly stronger than image-only with ResNet50 (0.725 vs 0.532 accuracy). Multiprofile avgpool gave no gain over single-profile for RNA (0.721 vs 0.725), a gap too small to read much into. The biggest untested question is whether the image modality adds complementary signal when combined with RNA. 2. Test: config_016 is single-profile PCA RNA plus ResNet50 with simple concat fusion. It is exactly the union of the two tested single-profile unimodal baselines (config_001 and config_010), so any change from 0.725 can be attributed to adding the image modality, with no confound from aggregation or encoder choice. 3. Why now: this cleanly answers the high-impact question of whether multimodality helps, which governs most of the remaining search space. If it gains, we can then explore fusion type, image encoder and aggregation. If it does not, we can redirect the budget toward RNA encoder comparisons such as scVI and scGPT.

1. Evidence and uncertainty: RNA-only PCA is the strongest so far (0.725 single-profile, 0.721 with multiprofile avgpool). Image-only ResNet50 is weaker (0.532). 1. Evidence: RNA-only with PCA (config_001, 0.725 acc / 0.685 F1) is the best result so far. Multiprofile averaging (config_002) gave about the same result, so profile setting looks minor for now. 1. Evidence: The RNA representation has had the largest effect observed so far. In the single-profile setting, PCA_n2000 reached 0.725 accuracy and 0.685 F1, while scVI_n200 reached only 0.530 accuracy, a gap of about 0.19. Other choices mattered much less. Multiprofile avgpool was essentially equal to single-profile (0.721). Adding ResNet50 images through weighted fusion lowered accuracy to 0.688, and concat fusion failed at 0.208. RNA-only with PCA is the current best, and the third RNA encoder, scGPT, is completely untested. 2. Test: config_007 changes only the RNA encoder to scGPT, keeping rna_only and single-profile fixed. This gives a clean comparison against config_001 (PCA) and config_004 (scVI), and shows whether a foundation-model embedding beats the current PCA baseline. 3. Value: The encoder is the design choice with the largest demonstrated impact. scGPT is the main unexplored option on the strongest modality and could raise the performance ceiling. The result also shapes the remaining budget: if scGPT wins, the multiprofile and multimodal scGPT variants become the priority; if it loses, PCA is confirmed and the budget can go to aggregation (transformer) or the ViT-L image encoder. Aggregation and fusion changes have so far shown small or negative effects, so testing them first would be less informative.

This makes it the most uncertainty-reducing experiment for the remaining budget.

1. Evidence: PCA_n2000 is clearly the strongest RNA encoder, reaching 0.725 accuracy single-profile, versus about 0.53 for scVI and scGPT. Multiprofile has not helped so far: avgpool was roughly neutral at 0.721, and the transformer was clearly worse at 0.599. Among image encoders, ImageNet ViT-L beat ResNet50 (0.579 vs 0.532 accuracy, with F1 following the same pattern). In multimodal models, concat fusion collapsed to 0.208. Weighted fusion with ResNet50 reached 0.688, which is still below RNA-only. The main open question is whether any multimodal setup can beat RNA-only, or whether the weaker image signal mainly adds noise. 2. Test: config_023 keeps the best previously tested multimodal setup (single-profile, PCA_n2000, weighted fusion) and changes only the image encoder from ResNet50 to ViT-L. This isolates whether the stronger image representation improves fusion enough to close or reverse the gap to RNA-only. 3. Why now: This is a one-variable extension of the most promising multimodal result, so it combines exploitation with a clean test. It also decides whether the many remaining ViT-L multimodal configurations are worth budget. It avoids concat, which looks unstable from a single result, and avoids multiprofile aggregation, which has shown no benefit yet.

Transformer aggregation added a smaller gain (0.678 accuracy, 0.646 F1), so it is the best setting so far. The image-only ResNet50 single-profile model was weak (0.227), so it is unclear whether images will add value. 1) Evidence: RNA is clearly the dominant modality. RNA-only reached 0.421 accuracy versus 0.227 for image-only in single-profile. Multiprofile aggregation gave large gains (pca avgpool 0.653, pca transformer 0.678 / F1 0.646, the current best). Adding ResNet50 images with concat fusion lowered performance to 0.599. Evidence: Multiprofile aggregation clearly helps RNA-only models (0.42 single-profile vs 0.65 avgpool and 0.68 transformer). scVI is the best RNA encoder so far (0.725). Images alone are weak (ResNet50 0.227). Adding ResNet50 images through concat fusion lowered accuracy from 0.678 to 0.599 (config_003 vs config_020). That drop is a single result, so it is unclear whether multimodality itself hurts or whether concat fusion lets a noisy image signal degrade the RNA representation. Test: config_021 is identical to config_020 except that it uses weighted fusion instead of concat. This isolates the effect of the fusion method, and it can show whether weighted fusion learns to down-weight the weak image branch and recover or exceed RNA-only performance. Why now: The answer decides how to spend much of the remaining budget, since most untested configurations are multimodal. If weighted fusion still underperforms RNA-only, we can largely drop multimodal ResNet50 options and focus on scVI-based RNA models or test a stronger image encoder. If it helps, scVI with weighted fusion becomes a logical next step.

1) Evidence: Multiprofile aggregation clearly helps, roughly +0.23 to +0.25 accuracy over single-profile for PCA RNA, and transformer aggregation slightly beats avgpool. Among RNA encoders, scVI is the strongest so far (0.725 vs 0.678 for PCA under the same transformer setting), while scGPT is poor. Adding ResNet50 images with weighted fusion improved the PCA transformer model (0.713/0.695 vs 0.678/0.646), whereas concat fusion hurt it (0.599). This suggests that weighted fusion lets the model use weak image signal without being dragged down by it. 2) Test: config_033 changes only the RNA encoder from config_021 (PCA to scVI). It also differs from the current best, config_006, only by adding ResNet50 images with weighted fusion. So it shows whether the fusion gain seen with PCA carries over to the stronger scVI representation, or whether scVI already captures what images add. 3) Why now: it directly exploits the two most promising findings (scVI and weighted fusion), is the most likely candidate to beat 0.725, and cleanly isolates whether the image modality adds value, which is a central open design question.

1. Evidence: The best result so far is RNA-only scVI with a transformer (0.725 acc). Fusion results are mixed. With PCA RNA, weighted fusion with ResNet50 improved over RNA-only (0.713 vs 0.678, F1 0.695 vs 0.646), and weighted beat concat (0.599). With scVI RNA, the same weighted fusion with ResNet50 fell sharply (0.530). The image encoder is the largest untested design dimension: every image run used ResNet50, which is weak on its own (0.227 single-profile). 2. Test: config_027 keeps everything from config_021 (PCA, multiprofile, transformer, weighted fusion) and changes only the image encoder to ImageNet ViT-L. This isolates whether a stronger image representation adds more complementary signal in the fusion setup that has worked best so far. 3. Why now: It is a one-variable change from a strong multimodal baseline, so it is both exploitative and directly informative. A gain would justify exploring ViT-L further, including retrying scVI fusion. No gain would suggest image features add little and point the search back toward RNA-only refinement.

Only PCA (0.650 RNA-only) has been tried, so the RNA branch may be what drags fusion down. 2) This experiment swaps PCA for scVI (n200) in the single-profile RNA-only setting and changes nothing else. That isolates the effect of RNA representation quality. 3) With 2 experiments left, this is the most informative single-factor test. 1) Evidence: the best result so far is image_only single-profile ResNet50 at 0.721 accuracy (F1 0.681). The other directions have not beaten it. 1. Evidence: The best result so far is single-profile ResNet50 image-only (0.721 acc, 0.681 F1). Adding the RNA modality hurt in both fusion variants (concat 0.527, weighted 0.579). 1) Evidence: the best result so far is image-only, single-profile, ResNet50 (acc 0.518, F1 0.484). It beats RNA-only PCA (0.422). 1. Evidence: Image-only models are strongest so far, with ViT-L at 0.535 and ResNet50 at 0.518. RNA-only PCA is weaker at 0.422. 1) Evidence: Weighted fusion is the current best at 0.579 (config_017, pca_n2000 + resnet50, singleprofile), and concat fusion with the same encoders failed badly at 0.224. 1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_023 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l, weighted fusion) at 0.713 accuracy and 0.695 F1. Test: This swaps only the RNA encoder to scvi_n200 and keeps the best image encoder, single-profile setting and weighted fusion. 1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_023 (PCA RNA + ViT-L image, single profile, weighted fusion) at 0.713 accuracy and 0.695 F1. 1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_023 (PCA RNA + ViT-L image, single-profile, weighted fusion) at 0.713 accuracy and 0.695 F1. 1. Evidence: No experiments have been run yet, so we know nothing about which modality, RNA encoder, profile setting, aggregation, or fusion method works best. 2. Test: config_018 keeps config_002 unchanged (RNA pca_n2000, multiprofile, avgpool) and only adds a resnet50 image encoder with simple concat fusion. Why now: Whether to use images splits the remaining search space roughly in half, so answering it early best focuses the remaining 7 experiments. This isolates the effect of the profile setting. 3) Why now: profile setting applies across the RNA-only, image-only and multimodal branches, so learning whether multiprofile helps tells us how to weight most of the remaining 49 configurations. Using avgpool, the simplest aggregator, avoids mixing in the transformer's added complexity. A single-variable change against the only baseline is the most informative way to reduce uncertainty early in the budget. Encoder, image and fusion comparisons can follow once this is settled.

1) Evidence so far: with the PCA RNA encoder, going from single-profile to multi-profile with avgpool raised validation accuracy from 0.591 to 0.639, and F1 rose with it. That makes config_002 the current best. The image modality has not been tested at all, which is the largest open question in the search space. 2) This experiment keeps the best setup fixed (pca_n2000, multiprofile, avgpool) and adds ResNet50 image features with simple concat fusion. It asks whether image information adds value on top of the best RNA configuration. Adding a modality necessarily brings in an image encoder and a fusion method, so concat is used as the simplest fusion choice to keep the comparison clean. 3) Most untested configurations are multimodal, so whether images help or hurt is the decision that most shapes the remaining 7 experiments. If it helps, later runs can tune the image encoder, fusion, and aggregation. If it does not, the budget can go to RNA encoders (scvi, scgpt) and aggregation choices within RNA-only models. Comparing aggregation (config_003) or RNA encoders right now would refine one branch while leaving this bigger uncertainty open.

1. Evidence: The best result so far is RNA-only multiprofile with PCA and avgpool (0.639 accuracy, 0.620 F1). Moving from single-profile to multiprofile helped by about 5 points. Adding ResNet50 images with concat fusion hurt badly (0.518). That suggests the image branch, or naive fusion, adds noise for now. The RNA representation is still completely untested and is likely a major lever. 2. Test: This run keeps the best setup fixed (RNA-only, multiprofile, avgpool) and swaps only the PCA encoder for scVI. Any change in accuracy can then be attributed to the RNA encoder alone. 3. Why now: The RNA encoder choice carries forward to every later RNA-only and multimodal configuration, so settling it early makes the remaining six experiments more useful. scVI latents often capture cell-state structure better than PCA, which gives a realistic chance of beating 0.639. Testing scGPT and transformer aggregation can follow once this is known.

1) Evidence: the best result so far is config_002, an RNA-only multiprofile model with the pca_n2000 encoder and avgpool aggregation (accuracy 0.639, F1 0.620). Moving from single-profile to multiprofile with PCA added about 5 points. Swapping PCA for scVI under the same setup lowered accuracy to 0.573. Adding resnet50 images with concat fusion dropped performance sharply to 0.518. Aggregation is the main design choice not yet tested: only avgpool has been tried. 2) This experiment keeps everything in config_002 fixed and changes only avgpool to transformer aggregation. That isolates whether learned attention over profiles beats simple mean pooling on the strongest backbone found so far. 3) It is a one-variable extension of the current best, so the result is easy to interpret and has a good chance of raising the best accuracy. It also tells us which aggregation to carry into later tests of scGPT or other fusion settings with the 5 experiments that remain.

1) Evidence: RNA-only multiprofile models are strongest so far. PCA with transformer aggregation (config_003, 0.653 accuracy) narrowly beats PCA with avgpool (0.639). scVI underperformed PCA under avgpool (0.573). Multimodal concat with ResNet50 hurt performance substantially (0.518). The main untested uncertainty on the RNA side is the scGPT encoder, which may give a stronger representation than PCA. 2) This experiment keeps the best-known setup (RNA-only, multiprofile, transformer aggregation) and changes only the encoder from PCA to scGPT. That isolates whether a pretrained foundation-model embedding improves on PCA. 3) The RNA representation is the factor most likely to raise the current best, and this single-variable change exploits the strongest configuration while exploring an untested encoder. Weighted fusion or image-only runs remain options for later in the budget.

1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_003 (RNA-only, PCA, multiprofile, transformer) at 0.653 accuracy. PCA clearly beats scVI and scGPT, and the transformer slightly beats avgpool, though that gap is small. The only multimodal run, config_018, used concat fusion with avgpool and dropped to 0.518. That drop could come from the image features or from naive concat letting a noisy image signal swamp the RNA signal. 2. Test: config_021 keeps the best RNA setup (PCA, multiprofile, transformer) and adds ResNet50 image features through weighted fusion. Weighted fusion can down-weight an unhelpful modality, so this checks whether images add anything once the fusion method is not the bottleneck. Compared with config_003, the change is adding the image modality with weighted fusion. 3. Why now: With 3 experiments left, this is a direct extension of the current best and has a realistic chance of beating it. It also settles the main open question, whether multimodality helps at all, before any budget goes to image-only or other image-encoder variants.

1) Evidence: PCA_n2000 is clearly the strongest RNA encoder (scVI and scGPT were both worse). Multiprofile beats singleprofile, and transformer aggregation is slightly better than avgpool. The two best runs are close: RNA-only transformer (config_003, 0.653) and multimodal PCA+ResNet50 with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_021, 0.650). Concat fusion with avgpool performed poorly (0.518), so weighted fusion looks like the safer choice. The image encoder is still untested, since only ResNet50 has been tried. 2) This run keeps everything from config_021 the same and swaps ResNet50 for ImageNet ViT-L. That isolates whether a stronger image representation lets the multimodal model beat the RNA-only best. 3) With only 2 experiments left after this one, this is a single-variable change to a near-best configuration. It addresses the largest remaining uncertainty (image representation quality) and has a realistic chance of producing a new best accuracy. Low-yield directions such as scGPT or scVI, or lower-performing setups such as singleprofile and concat fusion, are less promising.

1. Evidence: The best results so far use the PCA RNA encoder with multiprofile transformer aggregation. RNA-only (config_003) reached 0.653 and multimodal ResNet50 with weighted fusion (config_021) reached 0.650, with nearly identical F1. scVI and scGPT were clearly worse, and ViT-L hurt performance. The open question is fusion type. Concat fusion has only been tried with avgpool (config_018, 0.518), so its poor result may come from the weak aggregator rather than from concat itself. 2. Test: config_020 keeps the PCA + ResNet50 + transformer setup and changes only the fusion, from weighted to concat. This isolates whether concat is harmful in general or can beat weighted fusion under transformer aggregation. 3. Why now: Lower-ranked alternatives such as scVI with transformer, or avgpool with weighted fusion, are unlikely to exceed 0.653 given current trends. config_020 is the remaining one-factor change with a real chance of a new best. If it fails, the final experiment can still exploit the weighted or RNA-only transformer direction.

1) Evidence: The best result so far is config_003 (RNA-only, PCA, multiprofile, transformer) at 0.653 accuracy. The fusion method decides whether multimodal models work. With the PCA + ResNet50 transformer setup, weighted fusion (config_021) reached 0.650, but concat fusion (config_020) dropped to 0.540. Concat fusion also did poorly with avgpool (config_018, 0.518). Weighted fusion appears to let the model reduce the influence of the image modality, which avoids the losses seen with concat. The scVI and scGPT encoders and the ViT-L image encoder have all been clearly worse, and single-profile is worse than multiprofile. 2) This experiment tests whether weighted fusion with ResNet50 also rescues the avgpool multimodal model. It completes the fusion-by-aggregation comparison for the strongest encoder pair (PCA + ResNet50). 3) This is the final experiment, so the aim is the best chance of a top score. Every candidate using scVI, scGPT or ViT-L is strongly predicted to underperform. config_019 keeps the best encoders and multiprofile and changes only one choice relative to the tested weighted multimodal config_021. Its plausible range (about 0.63–0.66) gives it a realistic chance to match or beat the current best.

1. Evidence/uncertainty: No experiments have been run, so we know nothing yet about which modality, encoder, profile setting, aggregation or fusion works best. 2. What this tests: config_001 (RNA-only, single-profile, PCA-2000) is the simplest configuration. It has no aggregation or fusion parts, so it gives a clean reference accuracy and F1. Later runs can change one factor at a time against it: the RNA encoder (scVI, scGPT), the profile setting and aggregation (avgpool, transformer), or the modality (image-only, multimodal). This lets us attribute any gains to a specific design choice. 3. Why now: With 10 experiments, a well-defined anchor at the start makes every later comparison easier to interpret. This avoids assuming that complex multimodal or multi-profile models are better and keeps the search efficient.

1) Evidence: there is only one result, the RNA-only singleprofile PCA baseline (val acc 0.519, F1 0.480). Nothing yet shows how the major design axes (profile setting, encoder, modality) affect performance. 2) Test: config_002 keeps the same RNA-only PCA setup and changes one thing, singleprofile to multiprofile with simple avgpool aggregation. This isolates whether aggregating multiple profiles helps. 3) Why now: profile setting is a key choice that applies across modalities and could shape the many multiprofile configurations still available. Avgpool is the simplest aggregation, so a gain can be credited to multiprofile input rather than to a more complex aggregator. The result will guide whether later experiments focus on multiprofile variants or on encoder and modality comparisons.

1) Evidence: Both experiments so far are RNA-only PCA. Singleprofile (0.519 acc) and multiprofile avgpool (0.518 acc, slightly higher F1) are essentially tied, so with avgpool the profile setting has little effect for PCA RNA. The image modality is completely untested, and it is the largest open question in the search space. 2) Test: config_010 runs image-only singleprofile with the ResNet50 encoder. It is the image counterpart of the config_001 baseline, so the comparison isolates modality while keeping profile setting and aggregation fixed. 3) Why now: Most of the remaining space is multimodal. Knowing whether images alone are weaker, comparable or stronger than RNA (~0.52) will guide whether to spend later experiments on fusion, image encoders, or RNA encoders such as scVI and scGPT. This early, a broad test that cuts uncertainty about a major design choice is worth more than small tweaks to the PCA RNA baseline.

Evidence: image-only ResNet50 single-profile scored highest (0.532 acc, 0.516 F1). It edges out RNA-only PCA (0.519). Multiprofile avgpool for RNA made almost no difference (0.518 vs 0.519). The biggest untested question is whether combining the two modalities helps at all. This experiment tests the simplest multimodal model: concat fusion, single-profile, using the same PCA and ResNet50 encoders already measured alone. Because both unimodal baselines are known, any gain or loss is attributable to fusion itself. It is the best next step because multimodal configurations make up most of the search space. Knowing early whether fusion adds value will guide whether the remaining 6 experiments go to multimodal variants (encoders, weighted fusion, aggregation) or to unimodal image encoders such as ViT-L.

1) Evidence: the image-only ResNet50 single-profile model is the best so far (acc 0.532, F1 0.516). Its F1 lead over every RNA-based run is clearer than its small accuracy lead. Adding PCA RNA through concat fusion (0.520) and multiprofile avgpool for RNA (0.518) gave no gain, so the image branch looks like the main signal source. The image encoder choice is still completely untested. 2) This experiment swaps ResNet50 for ImageNet ViT-L and keeps everything else fixed (image-only, single-profile). That isolates the effect of the image representation. 3) It exploits the strongest direction while settling a key design choice. The result also tells us which image encoder to carry into the remaining multiprofile, aggregation and fusion experiments, which makes the rest of the budget more efficient.

Evidence: image-only ResNet50 single-profile (config_010) is the current best, at 0.532 accuracy and 0.516 F1. RNA PCA scores about 0.52 whether single-profile or multiprofile with avgpool. Concat fusion of PCA and ResNet50 (0.520) did not beat ResNet50 alone, which suggests the RNA branch may be diluting the image signal. ViT-L performed very poorly. Question: config_011 changes only the profile setting, testing multiprofile with simple avgpool on the strongest representation, ResNet50. This isolates whether multiprofile helps image features, since it was neutral for RNA. Why now: it builds directly on the strongest result with a single-factor change. Its outcome will guide the remaining budget. If multiprofile helps, I can try transformer aggregation or multimodal multiprofile variants. If it does not, I can turn to untested RNA encoders (scVI, scGPT) or weighted fusion.

1. Evidence: The best result so far is single-profile ResNet50 image-only (acc 0.532, F1 0.516). Single-profile PCA RNA-only scores 0.519. Concat fusion of these two (config_016) scores 0.520 with F1 0.479. That is essentially RNA-level performance, which suggests concatenation lets the high-dimensional RNA features dominate rather than adding complementary signal. Multiprofile avgpool gave no clear gain for either modality, and ViT-L image features performed poorly. 2. Test: config_017 keeps everything from config_016 the same and changes only concat to weighted fusion. This isolates whether the fusion method is what blocked a multimodal gain, for example by letting the model weight the stronger image modality. 3. Why now: Multimodal fusion is the only direction where the two strongest components could combine to exceed 0.532. This single-variable test settles the fusion question cheaply. That leaves 2 experiments either to extend weighted fusion (for example a different RNA encoder or transformer aggregation) or to fall back to the image-only path.

1) Evidence: The best result so far is image-only ResNet50 single-profile (0.532 accuracy, 0.516 F1). PCA RNA is close behind (0.519). Concat fusion with PCA RNA (0.520) did not beat image alone, and weighted fusion hurt (0.435). Multiprofile avgpool gave no gain for either modality. The largest untested axis is the RNA encoder: scVI and scGPT have not been tried at all. A weak PCA representation may be what limits both RNA-only and fusion performance. 2) Test: scGPT RNA-only single-profile changes only the encoder relative to config_001. This isolates whether a pretrained foundation-model embedding beats PCA. 3) Why now: If scGPT clearly improves on PCA, the last experiment can exploit it directly with scGPT+ResNet50 concat (config_040), the combination with the most upside. If it does not, the last slot can go to refining the image-only path, such as transformer aggregation (config_012). This choice reduces the most important remaining uncertainty while keeping a clear final exploit step.

1) Evidence: The RNA encoder is the strongest factor found so far. scGPT single-profile RNA-only reached 0.586 accuracy and 0.574 F1, well above PCA (about 0.519) and ResNet50 image-only (0.532). Multiprofile avgpool did not help either PCA RNA or ResNet50 images. Weighted fusion hurt badly (0.435). Concat fusion with PCA and ResNet50 roughly matched the unimodal results without degrading them. 2) This experiment: It changes one thing from the best configuration by adding ResNet50 image features with concat fusion while keeping scGPT single-profile. It tests whether the image modality adds information beyond the stronger scGPT representation, which the weaker PCA features may have masked before. 3) Why now: With only two experiments left, exploiting the best encoder is more valuable than exploring settings that have looked weak, such as ViT-L, weighted fusion or multiprofile pooling. Concat is the fusion method least likely to hurt, and ResNet50 is the best image encoder tested. That makes this the most plausible single step to beat 0.586.

Evidence: scGPT RNA-only single-profile (config_007, acc 0.586, F1 0.574) is clearly the best result so far. It beats PCA RNA-only (~0.52), every ResNet50 image-only run (≤0.532) and every multimodal fusion run (≤0.520). Adding images to scGPT reduced accuracy (config_040, 0.507), so further multimodal tests look unpromising. Multiprofile avgpool gave essentially no change for PCA (0.518 vs 0.519) and a slight drop for ResNet50 (0.523 vs 0.532). That suggests simple mean pooling is unlikely to add much on top of scGPT. Transformer aggregation has never been tested and is the main open question on the profile and aggregation axis. Test: config_009 keeps the best encoder (scGPT) and changes only the profile setting and aggregation, to see whether learned attention over multiple profiles can beat single-profile scGPT. Why it is the best use of the last experiment: only the best accuracy counts, and config_007 is already secured. A higher-variance extension of the strongest direction is therefore preferable to config_008 (avgpool), whose expected gain from prior evidence is near zero. It is also preferable to scVI or ViT-L options, which have no supporting evidence or performed poorly.

1. No experiments have been run yet, so there is no evidence about any design choice: modality, RNA or image encoder, profile setting, aggregation, or fusion. 2. This tests the simplest configuration, RNA-only with a single profile and PCA (n=2000) features. It sets a baseline for validation accuracy and F1. 3. A clean, low-complexity anchor is the best first use of the budget. Each later experiment can change one factor at a time against it, such as switching to the scVI or scGPT encoder, adding multiprofile aggregation, or adding images. That makes the effect of each choice easier to read, rather than assuming that more complex multimodal models will win.

1) Evidence: we have one result, the RNA-only single-profile PCA baseline (config_001: acc 0.678, F1 0.646). Nothing is known yet about profile setting, the other encoders, images, or fusion. 2) Test: config_002 keeps the same RNA-only PCA encoder and switches to multiprofile input with simple avgpool aggregation. This changes one design choice and isolates whether combining multiple profiles helps over a single profile. 3) Why now: profile setting runs through roughly two-thirds of the search space, including the multimodal configs. Using avgpool, the simplest aggregation, gives a clean answer before spending budget on transformer aggregation, other RNA encoders, image models, or fusion variants. Later experiments can then target the most promising branch.

1) Evidence: Only RNA-only PCA models have been tested. Single-profile scored 0.678 accuracy (F1 0.646) and multiprofile avgpool scored 0.653 (F1 0.628). That is a small sign that avgpool multiprofile does not help with PCA, though one comparison is not conclusive. The biggest open question is whether imaging adds anything, since the whole image and multimodal half of the search space is untested. 2) Test: config_016 adds ResNet50 image features to the current best setup (PCA single-profile) using simple concat fusion. Profile setting and RNA encoder stay fixed, so any change is attributable to adding the image modality. 3) Why now: This one experiment shows whether the multimodal branch, which holds most of the remaining configurations, deserves budget. If it beats 0.678, later runs can tune the image encoder and fusion. If not, the budget can go to RNA encoders (scVI, scGPT) and aggregation choices.

1. Evidence: RNA-only single-profile with PCA (0.678 acc, 0.646 F1) is the current best. Multiprofile avgpool was slightly worse (0.653). Multimodal concat with ResNet50 collapsed to 0.224, so naive image fusion currently hurts badly. The RNA encoder, the strongest signal source, has only been tested with PCA. 2. This experiment swaps PCA for scVI (n200) and keeps the best setting otherwise (RNA-only, single-profile, no aggregation or fusion). That isolates the effect of the RNA representation. 3. Improving the dominant RNA branch is the most likely route to a higher best accuracy. The result will also show which RNA encoder to carry into later multiprofile or weighted-fusion experiments. Probing why fusion failed matters, but improving on the current best through the RNA encoder comes first with 6 experiments left.

1) Evidence: the best result so far is single-profile RNA-only with PCA (config_001, acc 0.678, F1 0.646). Switching to scVI cut accuracy to 0.435. Multiprofile avgpool was slightly worse (0.653). Concat fusion with ResNet50 collapsed to 0.224. The RNA encoder clearly has the largest effect, but scGPT, the third encoder, is still untested. 2) This experiment changes only the encoder relative to config_001 (PCA to scGPT, still RNA-only and single-profile). It completes the encoder comparison and shows whether a pretrained foundation-model representation beats PCA. 3) The encoder choice is the factor most likely to move the best accuracy, and its answer decides which encoder the remaining aggregation and fusion experiments (transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) should build on. That makes it the best use of the remaining budget.

1. Evidence: PCA RNA-only single-profile (config_001, 0.678) is the clear leader. scVI and scGPT were much worse, and multiprofile avgpool (0.653) gave no gain. The one multimodal run, PCA + ResNet50 with concat fusion (config_016), collapsed to 0.224, far below RNA alone. A drop that large points to a fusion problem, such as the image features swamping or adding noise to the RNA signal, rather than to images carrying no information. 2. Test: config_017 keeps everything from config_016 and changes only the fusion, from concat to weighted. That isolates whether a learned weighting can recover the RNA signal and possibly add complementary image information. 3. Why now: about half of the remaining search space is multimodal, so learning whether the collapse is concat-specific tells us whether that branch is worth any of the last 4 experiments. It is also the most plausible way to beat 0.678, since multiprofile aggregation has so far given no benefit. If weighted fusion also fails, the remaining budget can go to the RNA-only PCA variants, such as transformer aggregation (config_003).

1) Evidence: PCA-2000 is clearly the strongest RNA encoder. It beats scGPT at 0.537 and scVI at 0.435. Single-profile RNA-only (config_001, 0.678 acc, 0.646 F1) is the current best. Multiprofile with avgpool (config_002) was slightly lower at 0.653 accuracy. Adding ResNet50 images did not help: weighted fusion reached 0.635 and concat collapsed to 0.224. The main untested choice on the strongest branch is transformer aggregation. Avgpool may simply have washed out profile-specific signal that a learned aggregator could keep. 2) Test: config_003 changes only one factor from config_002, aggregation (avgpool to transformer), holding PCA-2000, RNA-only and multiprofile fixed. It shows whether the multiprofile drop is due to the pooling method rather than to multiprofile itself, and whether it can beat config_001. 3) Why now: it stays on the highest-performing encoder and modality, and it isolates a single design choice. With 3 experiments left, it also tells me whether later runs should use multiprofile with transformer aggregation (including multimodal variants) or whether I should turn to the untested ViT-L image encoder with weighted fusion.

1) Evidence: the best result so far is RNA-only singleprofile PCA (0.678 accuracy, 0.646 F1). PCA clearly beats scVI and scGPT. Multiprofile pooling did not help, with avgpool slightly worse and the transformer collapsing. In multimodal runs, weighted fusion was far more stable than concat (0.635 vs 0.224), but adding ResNet50 images still fell short of RNA alone. 2) Test: keep the strongest settings fixed (PCA, singleprofile, weighted fusion) and change only the image encoder from ResNet50 to ImageNet ViT-L. This shows whether the multimodal deficit comes from weak ResNet50 image features or from fusion itself. 3) Why now: with 2 experiments left, this single change is the most plausible way to beat the RNA-only best. It avoids design choices that have already underperformed (concat, multiprofile, non-PCA encoders). The result will also tell us whether the final experiment should extend the ViT-L line or return to RNA-only variants.

Evidence: the best result so far is RNA-only PCA singleprofile (0.678 accuracy). PCA clearly beats scVI and scGPT. Transformer aggregation and concat fusion both collapse to about 0.22. Weighted fusion keeps multimodal models competitive: 0.635 with ResNet50 and 0.599 with ViT-L, and ResNet50 does better. Multiprofile with avgpool costs only a little (0.653 against 0.678). Uncertainty: neither weighted fusion nor avgpool multiprofile beat the RNA-only baseline alone. We have not tested whether combining the two non-collapsing choices, with the stronger PCA encoder and ResNet50, adds complementary signal. Test: config_019 (multimodal, multiprofile avgpool, PCA + ResNet50, weighted fusion) answers this directly. It reuses only components that have already worked and avoids the failed transformer and concat options. Why now: the other untested options are unlikely to exceed 0.678. Those include image-only models, the weaker RNA encoders, and anything with transformer aggregation or concat fusion. This makes config_019 the most plausible candidate to beat the current best, and it tells us whether the final experiment should continue down this multimodal multiprofile direction.

Evidence: the best result so far is RNA-only PCA single-profile (0.678). Every multimodal variant has fallen below it. Weighted fusion is clearly needed, since concat collapsed to about 0.22. Transformer aggregation also collapsed (0.227), which makes it a high risk on the final run. The scVI and scGPT encoders were much weaker than PCA. The only untested configurations that pair PCA with weighted fusion are 021 and 027, both transformer-based, and 025. This experiment tests whether ViT-L image features with multiprofile avgpool and weighted fusion beat ViT-L single-profile weighted (0.599). That would show whether profile pooling helps the ViT image branch. Multiprofile avgpool with ResNet50 and weighted fusion (0.629) stayed close to its single-profile counterpart (0.635), so a similar small effect is plausible here. This choice avoids the components that failed (concat, transformer) and the weak RNA encoders. It is still unlikely to beat 0.678, but it is the most plausible remaining candidate and also closes a gap in the ViT-L design comparison.

1) No experiments have been run yet, so there is no evidence about which modality, RNA encoder, profile setting, aggregation or fusion method helps. 2) config_001 is the simplest setup: RNA-only, a single profile, and PCA features with no aggregation or fusion. It gives a reference accuracy and F1 that later experiments can be compared against, one design choice at a time. Examples include swapping in scVI or scGPT, adding avgpool multiprofile aggregation, adding images, or using an image-only model. 3) With 9 experiments left, a baseline first makes each later result easy to read. It also guards against assuming that more complex multimodal or multiprofile models will automatically do better.

1. Evidence and uncertainty: there is only one result so far, an RNA-only single-profile PCA baseline at 0.332 accuracy and 0.315 F1. We do not yet know how informative the image modality is on its own, and that is the largest open question. It decides whether image encoders and multimodal fusion are worth spending the remaining budget on. 2. What this tests: config_010 is the simplest image counterpart to the baseline, using ResNet50, a single profile and no aggregation or fusion. Comparing it with config_001 shows which modality is stronger. The only change is modality, which by necessity also swaps the encoder. 3. Why now: this result gives the most guidance for the next 8 experiments. If images beat RNA, the search should prioritize image encoders and multimodal configurations. If images are weak, effort should go to RNA encoders and multiprofile aggregation. The profile setting and aggregation methods can then be tested cleanly within whichever modality proves stronger.

1. Evidence: Two single-profile baselines exist. Image-only ResNet50 (acc 0.471, F1 0.442) clearly beats RNA-only PCA (acc 0.332, F1 0.315). Image looks like the stronger modality, but we do not know whether the weaker RNA signal adds complementary information. 2. Test: config_016 keeps both tested encoders (PCA and ResNet50) and the single-profile setting, and adds only simple concat fusion. Any change from image-only is therefore due to adding RNA, not to a new encoder, profile setting or aggregation. 3. Why now: whether to fuse modalities is a major branch point. Over half the remaining configurations (36 of 49) are multimodal, so this answer decides where most of the remaining 7 experiments should go. If fusion helps, later runs can explore fusion type, encoders and multiprofile aggregation within multimodal models. If it does not, the budget can focus on image-only variants such as ViT-L or multiprofile ResNet50.

1. Evidence: The image-only model (0.471) clearly beat RNA-only (0.332). Concat multimodal fusion of PCA and ResNet50 is the best so far (0.518 accuracy, 0.484 F1), so combining modalities appears to help. Profile setting is still completely untested, and it is a major design axis that half of the remaining space depends on. 2. Test: config_018 keeps the best configuration fixed (PCA RNA, ResNet50 image, concat fusion) and changes only singleprofile to multiprofile, using the simplest aggregation (avgpool). This isolates whether multiprofile inputs add value. 3. Why now: The result decides whether the remaining 6 experiments should go to multiprofile variants (transformer aggregation, other encoders) or stay in singleprofile and focus on encoders and fusion. It builds on the current best result while resolving the largest open uncertainty.

1) Evidence: Image features carry most of the signal so far (image-only 0.471 vs RNA-only 0.332). Adding PCA RNA with concat fusion helps (0.518). Multiprofile avgpool adds almost nothing (0.520 vs 0.518, and F1 is slightly lower). The biggest open question is the image encoder, since every image result so far uses resnet50. 2) This run keeps the best simple setup fixed (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000 RNA, concat fusion) and swaps only resnet50 for imagenet_vit_l. That isolates the effect of the image representation, which has the most leverage on accuracy. 3) With 5 runs left, the encoder of the dominant modality is likely to matter more than small aggregation or fusion tweaks. The result will also tell me which image backbone to carry into later tests of RNA encoder (scvi or scgpt), transformer aggregation and weighted fusion.

1) Evidence and uncertainty: The image encoder is the dominant factor so far. Swapping resnet50 for imagenet_vit_l raised accuracy from 0.518 to 0.650, with F1 rising from 0.484 to 0.628. Multiprofile avgpool added almost nothing with resnet50 (0.520 vs 0.518, with lower F1). The RNA encoder is the largest untested design axis: every run used pca_n2000, and PCA RNA alone was weak (0.332). 2) What this tests: It keeps the best configuration (config_022: singleprofile, ViT-L, concat fusion) fixed and changes only the RNA encoder to the scgpt foundation-model embedding. This isolates whether a stronger RNA representation adds complementary signal on top of ViT-L. 3) Why now: Changing one variable from the current best both exploits the leading direction and resolves a major uncertainty. 1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_022 (PCA RNA + ViT-L image, single profile, concat fusion) at 0.650 accuracy and 0.628 F1. Two design choices clearly matter. 1) Evidence: The best result so far is config_006 (pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) at 0.635 accuracy and 0.618 F1. Several design choices look settled.
