The open questions are modality (RNA, image, or both), single vs. multi-profile input, encoder type, aggregation method and fusion strategy. 2. What this tests: config_030 is a mid-complexity multimodal anchor. It combines scVI RNA embeddings, ResNet50 image features, multiprofile avgpool aggregation and simple concat fusion. This gives an initial read on whether a multimodal, multiprofile pipeline works at all, without the extra variance from a transformer aggregator, weighted fusion or a large pretrained model. Each component can later be changed one at a time to isolate its effect: drop a modality (config_005 or config_011), switch to single-profile (config_028), use a transformer aggregator (config_032), use weighted fusion (config_031), or swap the encoders. 3. Why it is the best next experiment: With no prior evidence, a central baseline that has a reasonable chance of performing well yields both a usable score and many single-factor comparisons for later experiments. This uses the limited budget more efficiently than starting at either the simplest or the most complex corner of the search space.

1. Evidence: Only one experiment is complete. config_030 (multimodal, multiprofile, scVI, ResNet50, avgpool, concat) reached 0.208 accuracy and 0.172 F1. With a single data point, we cannot tell which component drives performance, or whether the image branch helps at all. 2. Test: config_005 keeps the scVI RNA encoder, multiprofile setting and avgpool aggregation, and removes only the image modality. This one-factor ablation measures the image branch's contribution directly. If RNA-only matches or beats the multimodal result, later experiments should focus on RNA encoders and aggregation. If it drops clearly, multimodal fusion is worth exploring, including ResNet50 vs ViT-L, concat vs weighted fusion, and transformer aggregation. 3. Why now: Whether multimodality is worthwhile is the highest-level design question in this space. Answering it first narrows the large remaining search space more efficiently than tuning lower-level choices such as aggregation or fusion under the current uncertainty.

Evidence: with scVI RNA, multiprofile and avgpool held fixed, adding ResNet50 images with concat fusion (config_030) dropped accuracy from 0.619 to 0.208, with F1 falling similarly. That is near-collapse, so the concat fusion step is the leading suspect. Uncertainty: we cannot yet tell whether the failure comes from the fusion method (concat letting noisy or high-dimensional image features swamp the RNA signal) or from the image modality itself. Test: config_031 changes only the fusion from concat to weighted, so it isolates the fusion effect. If weighted fusion recovers to RNA-only level or above, multimodal remains viable and the large multimodal search space is worth exploiting. If it still collapses, the evidence points to the image encoder or modality, and the next step would be image-only or ViT-L tests. Why now: this single-variable change resolves the most consequential open question, which is whether the multimodal branch deserves further budget.

1. Evidence: The RNA-only scVI multiprofile model with avgpool is clearly the best so far (acc 0.619, F1 0.610). Adding ResNet50 image features hurt performance, badly with concat (0.208) and moderately with weighted fusion (0.535). That gap is large enough to anchor further search on ViT-L. Aggregation, fusion and RNA encoder remain completely untested. 2. Swapping ResNet50 for ImageNet ViT-L, holding everything else fixed, raised accuracy from 0.41 to 0.59, a large and consistent gain in both accuracy and F1. Avgpool beat transformer aggregation (0.59 vs 0.52), though that rests on a single comparison. 1) Evidence so far: with multiprofile, multimodal PCA RNA, ViT-L beat ResNet50 by a wide margin (0.591 vs 0.411 accuracy). Avgpool beat transformer aggregation (0.591 vs 0.523). PCA beat scGPT, which dropped accuracy sharply to 0.224. 1) Evidence: The current best is config_025 (pca_n2000 + ViT-L + avgpool + weighted, acc 0.706, F1 0.667). Three design choices have each been tested once. The RNA encoder is the least resolved choice. scGPT did very poorly (0.224) in one concat run, and scvi_n200 has never been tested, so a major design choice is completely unexplored. 2) Test: Swapping PCA for scvi_n200 while keeping every other setting from the best configuration isolates the RNA encoder's effect in the strongest known context. Alternatives such as transformer + weighted (config_027) or single-profile variants refine choices that already have some evidence.

ViT-L clearly beats ResNet50 (0.59 vs 0.41). Avgpool beat transformer under concat (0.59 vs 0.52). Weighted fusion beat concat (0.706 vs 0.591, with F1 also higher). What this tests: config_004 changes only the profile setting relative to the current best (scVI, RNA-only, single-profile). It isolates the effect of multiprofile versus singleprofile on the strongest backbone found so far. 3. Why it is the best next use of budget: This axis affects roughly half of the remaining search space, including every singleprofile multimodal config. Resolving it prunes or prioritizes many configurations at once, while also offering a real chance of a new best. 1) Evidence and uncertainty: Multiprofile with avgpool is clearly the strongest setup. The best result is RNA-only scvi_n200 avgpool (0.713 accuracy, 0.695 F1), with scgpt close behind (0.706). Adding ResNet50 images lowered performance with both concat (0.635) and weighted fusion (0.688). Weighted fusion recovered most of the loss, which suggests the image features were adding noise. Only one image encoder has been tested, so it is unclear whether images are unhelpful in general or ResNet50 is just a weak encoder. 2) What this tests: config_037 keeps the best RNA backbone, multiprofile avgpool and the better fusion (weighted) fixed, and changes only the image encoder to imagenet_vit_l. 1. Evidence: The best results so far come from RNA-only models with multiprofile avgpool aggregation (scvi_n200 at 0.713 accuracy, scgpt at 0.706). Adding images has lowered accuracy in every run: resnet50 weighted fusion reached 0.688, concat 0.635, and ViT-L weighted 0.520. We have never tested images alone, so we cannot tell why fusion hurts. The image features may carry little signal, or the fusion step may be failing to use useful features. 2. Test: An image-only run with resnet50 and multiprofile avgpool, the strongest image setup seen so far, measures how much the image modality predicts on its own. 3. Why now: Most of the remaining options (over half) are multimodal, so this answer has high value. If image-only accuracy is near chance, we can drop most multimodal variants and focus the budget on RNA encoders and aggregation. 1) Evidence: Multiprofile avgpool aggregation is clearly the strongest pattern so far. RNA-only scvi_n200 reached 0.713 accuracy and scGPT reached 0.706. 1. Evidence: Multiprofile avgpool is clearly the strongest design. The top results are RNA-only scVI (0.713) and RNA-only scGPT (0.706). With the scVI/resnet50 pairing, weighted fusion beat concat (0.688 vs 0.635). Even so, the best multimodal run is still below RNA-only, so whether adding images helps at all is unresolved. Test: config_043 uses the best-known multimodal recipe (resnet50, avgpool, weighted fusion) with scGPT instead of scVI. 1. Evidence/uncertainty: No experiments have been run, so we have no evidence about which modality, encoder, profile setting, aggregation or fusion matters for this task. 2. What this tests: config_018 is a central, simple anchor point. It uses multimodal input, multiprofile with avgpool aggregation, concat fusion, and the simplest encoders (pca_n2000 and resnet50). 1. Evidence: Only one experiment has been run. config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, PCA RNA, ResNet50, avgpool, concat) gave a baseline of 0.520 accuracy and 0.479 F1. 1) Evidence: with everything else fixed (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000 + resnet50, concat), transformer aggregation beat avgpool by about 10 points in both accuracy (0.619 vs 0.520) and F1 (0.610 vs 0.479). 1. Evidence: Two single-factor comparisons point the same way. Evidence: Four experiments, all using concat fusion, point to transformer aggregation (+0.10 accuracy over avgpool with PCA/ResNet50), scGPT RNA embeddings (+0.11 over PCA) and ResNet50 over ViT-L (+0.05 with scGPT/transformer). The best so far is config_044 at 0.725 accuracy and 0.685 F1. Fusion strategy has never been varied, so it is the largest remaining uncertainty among the multimodal design choices. 1) Evidence: The best result so far is config_044 (scGPT + ResNet50 + transformer + concat, accuracy 0.725, F1 0.685). Single-variable comparisons favor transformer over avgpool aggregation (+0.10 with PCA), scGPT over PCA (+0.11), ResNet50 over ViT-L (+0.05), and concat over weighted fusion (+0.14). 1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_044 (scGPT + ResNet50, transformer aggregation, concat fusion), at 0.725 accuracy and 0.685 F1. The history points to several robust patterns. The RNA encoder matters most: scGPT beats PCA (0.619), which beats scVI (0.427). Transformer aggregation beats avgpool (0.620 vs 0.520 with PCA). Concat fusion beats weighted (0.725 vs 0.586). ResNet50 beats ViT-L (0.725 vs 0.678). The key untested question is whether the image modality adds anything at all. Every run so far has been multimodal, and the large swings from changing the RNA encoder suggest RNA may carry most of the signal. 2. Test: config_009 is the RNA-only version of the best setup (scGPT, multiprofile, transformer). It directly measures the image branch's contribution. If it matches or beats 0.725, multimodality is not helping, and the remaining budget should shift toward RNA-side choices. If it falls clearly below, the image branch is earning its place, and further image or fusion tuning is justified. 3. Why now: This one ablation resolves the most basic open design decision (modality setting), which affects how the rest of the budget is spent. It also has a realistic chance of matching the current best, so it serves both exploration and exploitation.

1) Evidence: The other design choices have each been compared at least once, all within the multiprofile setting. Transformer aggregation clearly beat avgpool (0.62 vs 0.52 with PCA). scGPT was the best RNA encoder (0.72, vs 0.62 for PCA and 0.43 for scVI). ResNet50 beat ViT-L (0.72 vs 0.68). Concat fusion beat weighted fusion (0.72 vs 0.59). Multimodal far exceeded RNA-only (0.72 vs 0.33). Profile setting has never been varied, so whether multiprofile modeling is needed is the largest open question about a core design choice. 2) Test: config_040 takes the current best stack (scGPT + ResNet50 + concat) and switches it to the single-profile setting. Comparing it with config_044 isolates the effect of multiprofile modeling with transformer aggregation. 3) Why now: This contrast fills the one untested dimension, anchored to the strongest configuration so far. A comparable or better result would open the cheaper single-profile branch (configs 016, 022, 028, 046, etc.) for further search.

1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_044 (scGPT + ResNet50, transformer, concat; 0.725 accuracy, 0.685 F1). Matched comparisons favor multiprofile over singleprofile, concat over weighted fusion, ResNet50 over ViT-L, and scGPT over PCA and scVI. The RNA-only scGPT transformer reached only 0.332 accuracy. 1) Evidence: The best result so far is config_044 (scGPT + ResNet50 + transformer + concat, 0.725 accuracy, 0.685 F1). 1. Evidence: No experiments have been run yet, so there is no evidence about which design choices matter: modality, single vs. multi-profile, RNA encoder, image encoder, aggregation, or fusion. 2. What this tests: config_030 is a central anchor. 1. Evidence: there is only one result so far, the multimodal multiprofile scVI + ResNet50 avgpool concat model (config_030) at 0.540 accuracy and 0.524 F1. A single point cannot tell us whether the image branch and fusion add anything. 2. Test: config_005 removes only the image modality and keeps the same RNA encoder (scVI), multiprofile setting and avgpool aggregation. Evidence: with the same scVI RNA encoder and multiprofile avgpool setup, adding ResNet50 images with concat fusion (config_030, acc 0.540, F1 0.524) did much worse than RNA-only (config_005, acc 0.688, F1 0.659). 1. Evidence: RNA-only with scVI and avgpool (config_005) reached 0.688 accuracy and 0.659 F1. 1. Evidence: The best result so far is RNA-only, multiprofile, scVI with avgpool (0.721 accuracy, 0.681 F1). That leaves the RNA encoder as the largest unexplored choice within the most promising region. 2. Test: config_002 keeps the winning setup (RNA-only, multiprofile, avgpool) and swaps in pca_n2000. 1) Evidence: The best result so far is RNA-only scVI with avgpool on multiprofile data (config_005: accuracy 0.721, F1 0.681). 1) Evidence: The best result so far is config_050 (scGPT + ImageNet ViT-L, multiprofile, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) at 0.721 accuracy and 0.681 F1. Several choices already have support. 1. Evidence: only one run exists. config_030 (multimodal, multiprofile, scVI, ResNet50, avgpool, concat) reached 0.520 accuracy and 0.498 F1. 1) No experiments have been run, so there is no evidence about which design choices matter. That covers modality, single vs. multi-profile, RNA encoder, image encoder, aggregation and fusion. 2) Config_030 (multimodal, multiprofile, scVI-200, ResNet50, avgpool, concat) uses a middle-of-the-road setting on every factor: a compact learned RNA embedding, a standard image backbone, the simplest aggregation and the simplest fusion. It sets a baseline for the full multimodal pipeline, from which each factor can be tested by changing one thing at a time. Examples are switching to RNA-only (config_005) or image-only (config_011), single-profile (config_028), transformer aggregation (config_032), weighted fusion (config_031), or a different encoder (config_042 or config_036). 3) A unimodal baseline such as config_001 could tell us about only one branch. 1. Evidence: Only one run exists. Multimodal scVI + ResNet50 with avgpool and concat fusion reached 0.532 accuracy and 0.516 F1. One run gives no reference point, so we cannot yet tell which design choices drive performance. 2. What this tests: config_005 keeps the scVI encoder, multiprofile setting and avgpool aggregation, and removes only the image branch. This single-factor ablation shows whether the ResNet50 image features add anything over RNA alone. 3. Why now: Whether to fuse modalities at all is the most basic decision in the search space. The answer decides whether the budget should go to multimodal variants (image encoder, fusion type, aggregation) or to RNA-only refinement. It is more informative than tuning a secondary factor before we know if multimodality helps.

1. Evidence and uncertainty: Only two runs exist, both using scvi_n200 with avgpool aggregation. RNA-only had slightly higher accuracy (0.542 vs 0.532). Multimodal concat had noticeably higher F1 (0.516 vs 0.483). This hints that adding the image modality helps balanced class performance, but the accuracy gap is too small to read much into. Aggregation is untested: every run so far used avgpool. 2. What this tests: config_032 keeps everything from config_030 the same (multimodal, scvi_n200, resnet50, concat) and swaps only avgpool for transformer. This isolates the effect of the aggregation method. It does so in the multimodal setting, which has the strongest supporting F1 evidence. 3. Why it is the best next use of budget: Aggregation affects every multiprofile configuration, so resolving it early narrows the remaining search space a lot. Testing it on the more promising multimodal setting also gives a reasonable chance of a new best result, balancing learning with performance.

1. Evidence: Transformer aggregation lifted the multimodal scVI+ResNet50 concat model from 0.532 to 0.713 accuracy, with F1 rising from 0.516 to 0.695. Under avgpool, RNA-only (0.542) roughly matched multimodal (0.532), so it is unclear whether images add anything. 2. Test: config_006 is the RNA-only scVI multiprofile model with transformer aggregation. It is the direct ablation of the best run. If it nears 0.71, the gain comes mainly from the aggregation and images add little. If it stays well below, the image modality contributes under transformer aggregation. 3. Why now: Whether images help decides how much of the remaining budget should go to image-encoder and fusion choices (ViT-L vs ResNet50, weighted vs concat) or to RNA encoders with transformer aggregation. One run resolves this, which is a better use of budget than a local tweak to the current best.

Evidence: the best result so far is multimodal scVI + ResNet50 with transformer aggregation and concat fusion (0.713 accuracy, 0.695 F1). Swapping in avgpool drops this to 0.532. RNA-only with a transformer is poor (0.435), below RNA-only with avgpool (0.542). So the transformer gain appears only when image features are present, but we cannot yet tell whether it comes from the image modality itself or from combining the two. Test: image-only ResNet50 with multiprofile transformer aggregation isolates the image contribution under the best aggregation setting. If it approaches 0.71, images drive performance, and later experiments should focus on image encoders (e.g., ViT-L) and aggregation rather than RNA encoders or fusion. If it falls well short, combining modalities is what matters, and fusion type (weighted vs concat) and RNA encoder choice deserve the next experiments. Why now: one run resolves which modality drives the leading result. That guides how the remaining budget is split between image-side and RNA/fusion-side exploration, which is more informative than a single small tweak to config_032.

1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_032 (multimodal, scVI, ResNet50, transformer, concat) at 0.713 accuracy and 0.695 F1. It is far ahead of the avgpool multimodal run (0.532) and the unimodal baselines (0.43–0.54). Transformer aggregation with multimodal fusion therefore looks strongly promising. The image encoder has only been tested with ResNet50, and image-only ResNet50 was weak (0.494), so image representation quality is a major open uncertainty. 2. Test: config_038 keeps the winning setup fixed and swaps only ResNet50 for ImageNet ViT-L. This isolates whether a stronger image backbone improves the best pipeline. 3. Budget: It exploits the strong transformer-multimodal direction while answering one important, untested design question. A backbone swap plausibly affects performance more than the fusion choice (concat vs. weighted), so it is the most informative single-variable extension. Fusion type and RNA encoder can be tested next.

1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_032 (multimodal, scVI, ResNet50, transformer, concat) at 0.713 accuracy and 0.695 F1. Under concat fusion, the transformer clearly beat avgpool (0.713 vs 0.532) and ResNet50 beat ViT-L (0.713 vs 0.639). Multimodal also beat both single-modality baselines. The main uncertainty is fusion: weighted fusion has never been tested, so all multimodal conclusions so far depend on concat. 2. Test: config_033 changes only concat to weighted fusion in the best configuration. Any difference can therefore be attributed to the fusion method. 3. Value: This is a low-risk extension of the leading configuration that could beat it, and it resolves an entire untested design dimension in one run. That result will guide whether later multimodal runs (e.g., testing PCA or scGPT RNA encoders) should use concat or weighted fusion.

1) Evidence: The best result so far is config_032 (scVI + ResNet50 + transformer + concat, 0.713 acc / 0.695 F1). Three single-factor changes from it all performed worse. Swapping in ViT-L gave 0.639, weighted fusion gave 0.632, and avgpool aggregation gave 0.532. Multimodal transformer also clearly beats the unimodal runs. The RNA encoder is the one axis never varied. scVI is the only RNA encoder tested in any setting, so whether it is a good choice is the largest remaining uncertainty. 2) Test: config_044 keeps the winning setup (ResNet50, transformer, concat) and swaps only scVI for scGPT. Any difference can therefore be credited to the RNA representation. 3) Why now: This closes the last untested single-factor comparison around the current best. It could find a stronger configuration if the foundation-model embeddings help. 1) Evidence: The best result so far is config_032 (scVI + ResNet50 + transformer + concat, 0.713 acc, 0.695 F1). Each component has been varied once around it. Avgpool dropped accuracy to 0.532, ViT-L to 0.639, weighted fusion to 0.632 and scGPT to 0.224. The scGPT drop shows the RNA encoder is a very high-impact choice. The third option, PCA (pca_n2000), has never been tested in any setting. 2) This experiment changes only the RNA encoder to PCA and keeps the best image, aggregation and fusion settings. That makes it a better use of budget than further fusion or image-encoder variants, which already look inferior. Single-profile settings are the next untested question after this.

1) Evidence: Every completed experiment used the multiprofile setting. Within it, the best configuration so far is config_032 (scVI + ResNet50 + transformer + concat, 0.713 accuracy, 0.695 F1). That run clearly beat the avgpool version (0.532), weighted fusion (0.632), the ViT-L image encoder (0.639), the PCA RNA encoder (0.507) and the scGPT RNA encoder (0.224). It also beat the unimodal baselines. So the encoders, aggregation and fusion choices now have reasonable evidence. The profile setting is completely untested. 2) This experiment: config_028 keeps config_032's strongest components (scVI, ResNet50, concat) but switches to the single-profile setting, which has no aggregation. It directly tests whether multiprofile aggregation itself drives the gain, or whether a simpler single-profile model is competitive. The avgpool result (0.532) suggests aggregation choice matters a lot, so a single-profile baseline is needed to read that effect correctly. 3) Why now: further tweaks to fusion or encoders are unlikely to beat config_032 given the current evidence. 1) No experiments have been run yet, so we have no evidence on any design choice: modality (RNA, image, or multimodal), single- vs multi-profile input, encoder type, aggregation, or fusion. 2) config_018 is a simple, central multimodal anchor. It uses basic encoders (PCA RNA, ResNet50 image), simple avgpool aggregation and concat fusion, and sits on the multimodal/multiprofile branch that likely has the highest ceiling. 1. Evidence: Only one experiment has been run. config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000 + resnet50, avgpool, concat) reached 0.535 accuracy and 0.519 F1. With one data point, we cannot tell how much each component contributes. 2. What this tests: config_002 is a controlled ablation that changes one thing. It keeps the same RNA encoder, multiprofile setting and avgpool aggregation, but removes the image branch. This directly measures whether adding resnet50 images to concat fusion helps beyond RNA alone. 3. Why now: Modality is the most basic design choice in the space. If RNA-only matches config_018, the image encoder and fusion choices probably matter little, and later budget should go to RNA encoders (scvi, scgpt) and aggregation. If RNA-only is clearly worse, multimodal is confirmed as a real benefit, and later experiments can focus on image encoder (vit_l), aggregation and fusion. Either result cleanly prunes a large part of the search space.

1. Evidence: Two experiments share the same RNA encoder (pca_n2000), multiprofile setting and avgpool aggregation. Adding ResNet50 image features with concat fusion lowered validation accuracy from 0.639 (RNA-only) to 0.535, and F1 fell similarly (0.620 to 0.519). The open question is why. Either concatenation lets weaker or noisier image features dilute the RNA signal, or the image modality simply adds no useful information here. 2. Test: config_019 changes only one thing, swapping concat for weighted fusion. If accuracy recovers to or above the RNA-only baseline, fusion strategy is the bottleneck and the multimodal half of the search space stays worth exploring. If it stays near 0.535, image features are likely harmful in general, and the search should shift toward RNA-only variants such as other RNA encoders or transformer aggregation. 3. Why now: Fusion choice affects about half of the remaining configurations. A clean one-variable comparison with the existing multimodal run is the most efficient way to decide whether multimodal models deserve more of the limited budget.

1) Evidence: RNA-only (PCA, multiprofile, avgpool) is the best result so far at 0.639 accuracy and 0.620 F1. Both multimodal runs with ResNet50 did worse (0.535 and 0.512) under either fusion. So RNA appears to be the main source of signal, and these ResNet50 image features have not helped. The RNA encoder, which may matter a lot, has only been tested with PCA. 2) This run keeps the best setup (RNA-only, multiprofile, avgpool) and swaps PCA for scGPT. It tests whether a pretrained foundation-model RNA embedding beats PCA. 3) Since RNA carries most of the signal, the RNA encoder is the design choice most likely to move accuracy, and the result will guide which encoder to use in later multimodal runs. This is a better use of the budget than more fusion or aggregation variants built on the weak image branch.

1. Evidence: The best result so far is RNA-only PCA with multiprofile avgpool (0.639 acc, 0.620 F1). Adding ResNet50 images lowered performance under both concat (0.535) and weighted fusion (0.512), and scGPT was much weaker than PCA (0.435). Every multiprofile run so far used avgpool, so we do not know whether the aggregation method matters. 2. Test: config_003 changes only avgpool to transformer on the strongest baseline. This isolates the effect of aggregation and gives a clean, single-factor comparison. 3. Why now: Aggregation affects every multiprofile configuration, including all the remaining multimodal and image variants. Resolving it on the best-performing branch is both a reasonable exploitation step and a large reduction in uncertainty for future choices. It is a better use of the next run than testing image backbones or the scVI encoder first, since those will benefit from knowing which aggregator to use.

1) Evidence: The best result so far is RNA-only with PCA-2000, multiprofile and avgpool (acc 0.639, F1 0.620). The RNA encoder matters a lot: scGPT in the same setting scored about 0.20 lower. Adding ResNet50 images lowered performance (0.535 concat, 0.512 weighted), and transformer aggregation did worse than avgpool (0.537). The third RNA encoder, scVI-200, has not been tested at all. 2) Test: config_005 swaps only the encoder to scVI-200 and keeps every other setting from the best configuration. This isolates whether scVI can match or beat PCA. 3) Why now: The encoder is the factor with the largest observed effect, and scVI is its largest remaining unknown. The result could raise the best score directly, and it also decides which RNA encoder should carry into later multimodal and profile-setting experiments. That makes it more valuable than testing secondary choices such as fusion type or image backbone under an encoder that may not be the best.

1) Evidence and uncertainty: The best result so far is RNA-only PCA with avgpool on multiprofile input (0.639 accuracy, 0.620 F1). Swapping in other RNA encoders (scVI 0.494, scGPT 0.435), using transformer aggregation (0.537) or adding ResNet50 images (0.535 and 0.512) all did worse. Every run so far used multiprofile input, so we do not yet know whether multiprofile aggregation helps at all. It isolates the profile-setting effect, a major design axis with no data yet. 3) Why it is the best next use of budget: It cleanly answers a first-order question about the current best configuration. It also has a realistic chance of becoming the new best, which matters for exploitation. Whether to probe the image modality (for example image-only or ViT-L multimodal) can follow once the RNA baseline's profile setting is understood.

Evidence: pca_n2000 is clearly the strongest RNA encoder. It beats scVI and scGPT, and multiprofile avgpool (0.639) is the best result so far. Adding ResNet50 images lowered accuracy with both concat (0.535) and weighted fusion (0.512). The open question is why: is the image modality uninformative, or is ResNet50 a poor image encoder for this task? The other image encoder, imagenet_vit_l, has never been tested in any setting. This experiment keeps everything from the best multimodal setup (pca_n2000, multiprofile, avgpool, concat, which beat weighted) and swaps only the image encoder. That isolates whether image-encoder choice drives the multimodal penalty. If ViT-L closes or reverses the gap with RNA-only, the multimodal ViT-L configurations become worth exploring. If it does not, the image modality likely adds little, and the remaining budget can go to the RNA-only side. Either outcome resolves a major uncertainty, and the run also has a realistic chance of producing a new best, so it serves both exploration and exploitation.

1) Evidence: The best result so far is config_024 (PCA + ViT-L, avgpool, concat; acc 0.688, F1 0.659). It beats RNA-only PCA avgpool (0.639). By contrast, PCA + ResNet50 multimodal runs scored below RNA-only (0.512-0.535), so the gain depends strongly on which image encoder is used. Two patterns look consistent but rest on only one or two comparisons each: avgpool beat transformer aggregation for RNA-only, and concat beat weighted fusion with ResNet50. No image-only model has been tested, so it is unclear whether ViT-L image features carry most of the signal by themselves or whether the gain comes from combining them with RNA. 2) Test: Image-only ViT-L with multiprofile avgpool isolates the image branch under the best-performing aggregation. If it scores near 0.69, the image representation is the main driver, and RNA adds little at the current fusion settings. If it scores clearly lower, the two modalities are complementary, and further fusion and aggregation tuning on PCA + ViT-L (e.g., config_025 or config_026) is well justified. 3) Why now: This single run settles the attribution question behind the main design choice, whether to invest in multimodal fusion or in image encoders. That makes it more informative under the limited budget than a small fusion or aggregation tweak to config_024, which the current trends suggest is unlikely to give a large improvement.

1) Evidence: The best result so far is image-only ViT-L with multiprofile avgpool (0.725 acc, 0.685 F1). Adding PCA RNA via concat lowered it to 0.688, and ResNet50-based multimodal runs were much weaker (0.51 to 0.54). This points to the ViT-L image branch as the main source of performance. Aggregation is still uncertain: transformer aggregation underperformed avgpool once, for PCA RNA (0.537 vs 0.639). That is a single experiment on a different modality, so it may not transfer to image features. 2) Test: Swapping avgpool for transformer aggregation on the leading image-only ViT-L configuration isolates whether learned multi-profile aggregation helps the strongest branch. 3) Why now: This exploits the most promising direction while settling a key design choice. If transformer aggregation helps, it could raise the best accuracy and would change which multimodal variants (e.g. config_026 and config_027) are worth running. If it hurts, it confirms that avgpool generalizes across modalities, and later experiments can focus on fusion and RNA-encoder choices.

1. Evidence/uncertainty: No experiments have been run yet, so nothing is known about which design choices matter: modality, single vs. multiprofile, RNA encoder, image encoder, aggregation or fusion. 2. What this tests: config_036 is a central anchor point. It is multimodal and multiprofile, uses a moderately strong RNA encoder (scVI), a strong pretrained image encoder (ViT-L), simple avgpool aggregation and the simplest fusion (concat). Its result gives a plausible high-performing reference, though that is an expectation rather than evidence. 3. Why it is the best next step: Because the configuration sits in the middle of the design space, later runs can each change one factor from it. 1. Evidence: Only one experiment is complete. The multimodal model (scVI RNA + ViT-L image, multiprofile avgpool, concat fusion) reached 0.332 accuracy and 0.315 F1. With no comparison point, we cannot yet tell whether the image branch adds anything. That is the most basic open question in the design space, and it affects how the rest of the budget should be spent. 2. Test: config_005 keeps the RNA encoder, profile setting and aggregation the same and removes only the image modality. The result will show directly how much the image branch contributes, on both accuracy and F1. 3. Why now: A clean single-factor modality ablation is the highest-value question at this sparse stage. If RNA-only matches the multimodal model, later experiments should focus on RNA encoders and aggregation. If it falls clearly short, image encoders and fusion strategies deserve more of the budget. 1. Evidence: with the same scVI-n200 encoder, multiprofile setting and avgpool aggregation, RNA-only reached 0.653 accuracy and 0.628 F1. Adding ImageNet ViT-L image features with concat fusion dropped this to 0.332 accuracy and 0.315 F1. It is unclear whether the image modality is unhelpful or whether concat fusion is the problem, for example high-dimensional ViT features swamping the RNA signal. 2. Test: config_037 is identical to config_036 except it uses weighted fusion, so it isolates the fusion choice. If weighted fusion recovers or beats RNA-only performance, concat was the bottleneck and multimodal search remains promising. If it stays low, the image features themselves are likely the issue. 3. Value: fusion type affects every multimodal configuration, which is most of the remaining space. One controlled comparison here will guide many later choices more than testing another RNA encoder or aggregation would.

1. Evidence: RNA-only scVI with avgpool (config_005) reached 0.653 accuracy. Adding ImageNet ViT-L image features with the same RNA encoder and aggregation sharply reduced accuracy, to 0.332 with concat fusion and 0.494 with weighted fusion. F1 followed the same pattern. Weighted fusion was clearly better than concat, which suggests the model does better when it can down-weight the image branch. The open question is whether image data hurts in general or whether the ViT-L features are the problem. 2. Test: config_031 keeps everything the same as config_037 (multiprofile, scVI, avgpool, weighted fusion) and changes only the image encoder to ResNet50. This isolates the image-encoder effect within the better fusion strategy. 3. Why now: whether to keep pursuing multimodal models at all is the most consequential design decision, and it should be resolved before spending more budget on smaller choices like aggregation or RNA encoder. If ResNet50 multimodal approaches or beats RNA-only, the image branch is worth keeping with a better encoder. If it also underperforms, that is strong evidence to focus remaining experiments on RNA-only refinements such as transformer aggregation or scGPT.

1) Evidence: RNA-only with scvi_n200 and avgpool is clearly the best result so far (acc 0.653, F1 0.628). All three multimodal runs scored much lower (0.33–0.52), so adding image features appears to hurt in the current setup, especially with concat fusion. Comparing RNA encoders (scGPT, PCA) is the natural follow-up.

1. Evidence: RNA-only models with scvi_n200 clearly lead (0.653 with avgpool, 0.678 with transformer). Every multimodal run scored much lower (0.33 to 0.52), so adding images has hurt so far. Transformer aggregation gave a small but consistent gain in both accuracy and F1. The biggest untested design choice is the RNA encoder, since only scvi_n200 has been tried. 2. Test: config_009 keeps the strongest setup (RNA-only, multiprofile, transformer) and swaps in scGPT. This isolates whether a pretrained foundation-model encoder beats scVI. 3. Weighted fusion beat concat by a wide margin, and resnet50 with weighted fusion (config_031, 0.520) was the best multimodal run. For RNA-only, transformer aggregation beat avgpool. What this tests: config_033 keeps everything from the best multimodal run (scVI, resnet50, weighted fusion) and changes only the aggregation to transformer. Why this is the best use of the budget: the result decides whether the remaining multimodal transformer configurations are worth exploring. Adding images currently hurts, so further multimodal tuning is low-value for now. Within RNA-only, transformer aggregation beat avgpool for scVI (0.678 vs 0.653, supported by F1). scVI also beat scGPT under transformer (0.678 vs 0.639). The pca_n2000 encoder has never been tested, so the RNA encoder choice, a major design decision, is still only partly mapped. 2. Test: config_003 keeps the best-performing setup (RNA-only, multiprofile, transformer) and swaps in pca_n2000. 1. Evidence and uncertainty: RNA-only models clearly lead. The best is scvi_n200 with transformer aggregation (0.678 accuracy, 0.646 F1), and scvi_n200 has beaten both scgpt and pca_n2000. All four multimodal runs fell far below RNA-only (0.33–0.52), so adding images currently hurts. However, every run so far has used the multiprofile setting, so we have no evidence on whether aggregating multiple profiles helps at all. 2. What this tests: config_004 is the singleprofile counterpart of the best RNA-only setup, keeping the scvi_n200 encoder fixed. 1. Evidence and uncertainty: RNA-only models are clearly strongest. The best is scvi_n200 with transformer aggregation (0.678 accuracy, 0.646 F1), followed by scvi avgpool (0.653). Every multimodal run underperforms these, from 0.33 to 0.52 accuracy. However, no image-only model has been tested, so we do not know why fusion hurts. What this tests: config_011 runs the image-only branch with resnet50, multiprofile and avgpool. Why now: this closes the largest unexplored axis (image-only) with one controlled run. What it tests: config_030 (multimodal, multiprofile, scVI RNA encoder, ResNet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, concat fusion) is a central, moderately complex anchor. 1. Evidence: Adding ResNet50 image features to the scVI RNA model (config_030, acc 0.520) did not beat RNA-only scVI with avgpool (config_005, acc 0.520), and F1 was actually lower (0.479 vs 0.498). So the image modality has shown no value so far. It is unclear whether imaging is uninformative or ResNet50 is a weak image encoder. 2. Test: config_036 keeps everything in config_030 fixed (multiprofile, scVI, avgpool, concat) and swaps only ResNet50 for ImageNet ViT-L. This run instead resolves the main open question, whether multimodality matters at all, and that answer should guide how the rest of the budget is spent.

It also picks the simpler or mid-range option on each remaining axis: a compact scVI encoder rather than the extremes of PCA or scGPT, a standard ResNet50, avgpool rather than a transformer, and concat rather than weighted fusion. Examples are switching to rna_only or image_only, singleprofile, a transformer aggregator, weighted fusion, or a different encoder. 3) Under a limited budget, starting from a central anchor makes each later experiment a one-factor contrast. That maximizes what we learn per run while keeping a good chance of strong immediate accuracy.

1) Evidence: only one experiment has been run. config_030 (multimodal, multiprofile, scVI RNA, ResNet50 image, avgpool, concat) reached 0.260 accuracy and 0.222 F1. 1. Evidence: Adding ResNet50 image features with concat fusion (config_030, acc 0.260, F1 0.222) did much worse than the matched RNA-only scVI model (config_005, acc 0.422, F1 0.405). With only two runs, it is unclear whether the cause is the concat fusion (for example, high-dimensional image features swamping the 200-d scVI embedding) or the image modality itself. 2. Test: config_031 keeps everything from config_030 the same (scvi_n200, resnet50, multiprofile, avgpool) and changes only the fusion to weighted. This isolates the effect of the fusion method. Why now: this single controlled comparison resolves the most consequential open uncertainty, whether multimodal fusion can help at all. 1) Evidence: with the scvi_n200 + resnet50 multiprofile avgpool setup held fixed, weighted fusion scored 0.540 accuracy and 0.524 F1. 1) Evidence: Transformer aggregation clearly beats avgpool (0.650 vs 0.525 with PCA+ResNet50). scGPT is the strongest RNA encoder so far (0.706 vs 0.650 for PCA and 0.494 for scVI). 1) Evidence: The best result so far is config_044 (scGPT + ResNet50 + transformer + concat, acc 0.706, F1 0.667). Transformer aggregation clearly beats avgpool (PCA: 0.525 to 0.650). 1. Evidence: The two RNA-only PCA runs are close (single-profile 0.650, multiprofile avgpool 0.639), so profile setting has only a small effect so far. 1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_022 (multimodal, multiprofile, scVI, ResNet50, avgpool, concat), at 0.721 accuracy and 0.681 F1. 1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_022 (scVI + ResNet50, avgpool, concat; acc 0.721, F1 0.681). Changing any single component from it lowered performance. 1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_022 (scVI + ResNet50, multiprofile, avgpool, concat) at 0.721 accuracy and 0.681 F1. Several single changes from it hurt performance. 1. Evidence and uncertainty: The best result so far is config_022 (scVI + ResNet50, avgpool, concat; acc 0.72). 1. Evidence: no experiments have been run yet, so there is no information about which modality, encoder, profile setting, aggregation or fusion choice matters. 2. What this tests: a simple RNA-only, single-profile model with a PCA (2000) encoder sets a low-complexity reference point. 1. Evidence and uncertainty: Adding ResNet50 image features to PCA RNA (single-profile, concat fusion) raised validation accuracy from 0.485 to 0.653, and F1 rose similarly. 1. Evidence: Image features carry most of the signal so far. Image-only ResNet50 reached 0.635 accuracy, RNA-only PCA reached 0.485, and concat fusion of the two reached 0.653 accuracy (F1 0.628). 1. Evidence: Among single-profile models, multimodal pca_n2000 + resnet50 concat (config_030) is best at 0.653 accuracy. 1) Evidence and uncertainty: The best result so far is single-profile multimodal with PCA RNA, ResNet50 images and concat fusion (config_030, acc 0.653, F1 0.628). Evidence: the best result so far is config_030 (multimodal, single-profile, PCA + ResNet50, concat fusion) at 0.653 accuracy and 0.628 F1. 1. Evidence: The image branch drives most of the performance. Image-only ResNet50 single-profile reached 0.635, close to the best result (multimodal PCA+ResNet50 concat, 0.653), while RNA-only reached only 0.485. 1) Evidence: no experiments have been run yet, so there is no evidence about which design choices matter. 2) Test: config_022 is multimodal and multiprofile, with scvi_n200 + resnet50, avgpool aggregation and concat fusion. It sets a mid-complexity anchor using the simpler option for aggregation (avgpool) and fusion (concat). 1. Evidence and uncertainty: We have one result so far. config_022 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200 + resnet50, avgpool, concat) reached 0.208 accuracy and 0.172 F1. With nothing to compare it against, we cannot tell whether this is good, or whether both modalities are contributing. 2. What this tests: config_037 is the RNA-only version of the same setup, with the same multiprofile setting, scvi_n200 encoder and avgpool aggregation. Only the image branch and fusion step are removed, so the comparison isolates what the image modality adds. 1. Evidence: Adding ResNet50 image features to the scVI RNA model with concat fusion (config_022) dropped validation accuracy from 0.619 to 0.208, with F1 falling similarly. This is a severe degradation, and it is unclear whether the cause is a weak image signal or a fusion problem, such as concat letting noisy image features dominate. 2. Test: An image-only ResNet50 model under the same multiprofile setting and avgpool aggregation (config_002) isolates how much the image modality contributes on its own. 3. Why now: If image-only is also near chance, image features themselves are the bottleneck, and the next steps should be a different image encoder (ViT-L) or more RNA-side exploration. If image-only is reasonably good, the failure points to the concat fusion, which justifies testing weighted fusion (config_024). 1. Evidence: The multimodal scVI + ResNet50 avgpool model with concat fusion (config_022) reached only 0.208 accuracy. That is far below RNA-only (0.619) and image-only (0.422) using the same encoders and aggregation. So the drop comes from how the modalities are combined, not from weak inputs. The likeliest cause is concat fusion, though one run alone does not prove it. 2. Test: config_024 keeps everything identical and changes only concat to weighted fusion. If accuracy recovers toward or above the RNA-only baseline, concat is the bottleneck. If it stays low, the problem is more general to multimodal training in this setup. 3. Why now: Most remaining configurations are multimodal and split between concat and weighted fusion. The answer will guide which aggregation to use in later RNA-encoder, profile-setting and fusion experiments.

1) Evidence and uncertainty: All five completed experiments used the multiprofile setting. The best result so far is RNA-only with scvi_n200 and avgpool (config_037: 0.619 accuracy, 0.610 F1). 1. Evidence and uncertainty: The best result so far is RNA-only, multiprofile, scVI with avgpool (acc 0.619, F1 0.610). Evidence: the best result so far is RNA-only, multiprofile, scVI, avgpool (0.619 accuracy, 0.610 F1). Multimodal models have not beaten it. With scVI and ResNet50 under multiprofile avgpool, weighted fusion reached 0.535 and concat fell to 0.208. 1. Evidence/uncertainty: No experiments have been run yet, so we know nothing about which design choices matter. Representation, profile setting, aggregation and fusion are all open questions. 2. What this tests: config_001 is a simple, mid-complexity anchor. It uses RNA only, multiple profiles, the compact scVI encoder and plain average pooling, with no image branch and no fusion. 1. Evidence and uncertainty: only one experiment has been run, an RNA-only multiprofile model with scvi_n200 and avgpool (acc 0.650, F1 0.628). 1. Evidence: RNA-only (scVI, multiprofile, avgpool) reached 0.650 accuracy. Adding ResNet50 images with weighted fusion, with everything else unchanged, collapsed accuracy to 0.208. With only two runs, it is unclear whether the cause is uninformative ResNet50 image features or a failure of the weighted fusion mechanism. 2. Test: the image-only ResNet50 model under the same multiprofile and avgpool setting provides the missing unimodal baseline. 1. Evidence: The best result so far is RNA-only with pca_n2000, multiprofile, and avgpool (0.725 acc, 0.685 F1). It clearly beats the scVI and scGPT RNA encoders under the same setting. With scVI, adding ResNet50 images through concat fusion gave 0.591 acc, below RNA-only's 0.650. Weighted fusion collapsed to 0.208. So whether images help at all is still uncertain, and it may depend on RNA representation quality. 2. Test: This experiment adds ResNet50 images with concat fusion to the best configuration (config_024). Everything else stays the same: pca_n2000, multiprofile, avgpool. That makes it a clean one-variable test of whether multimodal fusion helps once the RNA representation is strong. It also replicates the scVI fusion comparison (config_001 vs config_031) with a second RNA encoder, so we can see whether the fusion penalty is consistent. 3. Why now: Whether to pursue multimodal models at all is the most consequential open decision. It determines whether the remaining budget should go to image encoders and fusion variants or to refining RNA-only models. Using the stronger concat fusion and the known ResNet50 encoder avoids mixing in other untested changes, such as ViT-L or transformer aggregation.

1. Evidence: PCA_n2000 is clearly the strongest RNA encoder so far (RNA-only avgpool reached 0.725 accuracy, above scVI at 0.650 and scGPT at 0.599). Avgpool beat transformer aggregation (0.650 vs 0.519 for scVI), and multiprofile beat singleprofile (0.650 vs 0.507). Concat fusion was far more stable than weighted fusion (0.591 vs 0.208 for scVI+ResNet50). Adding ResNet50 to PCA with concat (config_009, 0.715) roughly matched RNA-only PCA but did not beat it. The image branch has only been tested with ResNet50, which was weak alone (0.523). The image encoder is therefore the largest untested design choice. 2. Test: config_013 differs from config_009 only in swapping ResNet50 for imagenet_vit_l. This isolates the effect of image representation within the best-performing multimodal setup. It also clarifies whether the image modality can add value beyond RNA, or whether ResNet50 features were the bottleneck. 3. Value: a single-variable change in the strongest context does two things at once. It reduces uncertainty about an unexplored design axis, and it has a realistic chance of exceeding the current best. A clear gain would point toward ViT-L-based multimodal extensions. No gain would strengthen the case that RNA-only PCA is sufficient.

1. Evidence: no experiments have been run yet, so we know nothing about which design choices matter. The first run should be a reference point that later runs can each change in only one way. 2. Test: config_031 is a simple multimodal setup: multiprofile, PCA RNA encoder, ResNet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation and concat fusion. 1. Evidence and uncertainty: only one experiment exists. The multimodal, multiprofile model (PCA-2000 RNA, ResNet50 image, avgpool, concat) reached 0.411 accuracy and 0.378 F1. 1. Evidence: with PCA-2000 RNA, multiprofile and avgpool held fixed, RNA-only (0.471 acc, 0.442 F1) beat multimodal ResNet50 concat (0.411 acc, 0.378 F1). 1) Evidence: with multiprofile, PCA RNA, ResNet50 and avgpool held fixed, image-only scored best (acc 0.532, F1 0.516), RNA-only was next (0.471/0.442), and concat fusion was worst (0.411/0.378). 1. Evidence: Image-only (ResNet50, multiprofile, avgpool) is the best result so far (acc 0.532, F1 0.516). RNA-only PCA comes next (0.471). 1. Evidence: Image-only models lead so far. ViT-L with avgpool scored 0.540 accuracy (F1 0.524) and ResNet50 with avgpool scored 0.532. RNA-only PCA reached 0.471. 1) Evidence: single-profile image-only ViT-L (config_024, 0.713 accuracy) is far better than every multiprofile run, all of which score 0.33-0.54. 1. Evidence and uncertainty: The best result so far is image-only singleprofile with ViT-L (0.713 accuracy, 0.695 F1), far above every multiprofile run (at most 0.54). Every multimodal run with PCA RNA has done worse than the unimodal runs. The singleprofile multimodal run with PCA and ViT-L fell to 0.328. 1. Evidence: Singleprofile has beaten multiprofile in both modalities tested: image ViT-L 0.713 vs 0.540, and RNA PCA 0.586 vs 0.471. Image-only ViT-L singleprofile is the best result so far. 1. No experiments have been run, so we have no evidence about whether any design choice helps: modality, multiprofile aggregation, encoder type or fusion. 2. This tests the simplest setup: RNA-only, single-profile, PCA (2000 components), with no aggregation or fusion. It sets a reference accuracy and F1 that every later experiment can be compared against. With a limited budget, a cheap and easy-to-interpret anchor is more useful than jumping to a complex multimodal configuration. 1) Evidence: there is only one result so far. The RNA-only, single-profile PCA baseline reached 0.512 accuracy and 0.477 F1. 1. Evidence: With the PCA RNA-only setup, single-profile reached 0.512 accuracy and 0.477 F1. Multiprofile with avgpool dropped sharply to 0.332 accuracy and 0.315 F1.
